specification.objective: Implement issue #120 as a desktop-only collapsible icon rail in the shared TouchIn workspace shell, preserving the current branch's navigation and access rules.

requirements.statement: At widths of at least 1080px, users can toggle the persistent shared sidebar between its expanded 360px icon-and-label panel and an 88px icon-only rail; the active page receives the reclaimed width.
Both modes retain all authorized destinations, logout, active-route indication, accessible names, hover/focus tooltips, visible keyboard focus, and comfortable targets.
The collapsed rail retains the TouchIn brand mark and an accessible expand control; contextual summaries are hidden only while collapsed and return when expanded.

One shared session-scoped navigation state survives WorkspaceScaffold route changes, including Kanban; route transitions remain instant, and any manual width animation respects reduced-motion settings.
Below 1080px the existing mobile header and hamburger drawer remain unchanged and no desktop collapse control or rail is shown.

Collapsed state intentionally is not persisted across a full browser reload: starting expanded preserves label discoverability if viewport size changes, while state is retained across in-app route navigation. This is the explicit reload-persistence tradeoff for this issue.
Store the locked contract in docs/contracts/issue-120-collapsible-sidebar-v1.polis.json and verify that the repository copy is byte-for-byte identical to the external lock.
Validate the expanded and collapsed desktop UI, in-app route retention, and narrow/mobile behavior visually with CUA on the refreshed app.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The desktop toggle switches between expanded labels/context and an 88px icon-only rail, and the page content uses the freed width without clipping.
Collapsed destination and logout icons remain usable and expose their labels as tooltips and semantics; active selection and keyboard focus remain available.
The same collapsed state remains after navigating to another workspace route including /kanban, and expansion restores labels and contextual content without a route transition.
At 1079px the mobile drawer remains in use without a collapse control; at 1080px the desktop panel and toggle are available.
The shared state is session-scoped, route changes remain instant, and reduced-motion requests disable the optional manual width animation.
The repository contract copy is byte-for-byte identical to the external locked contract.
CUA visual review confirms the desktop rail, expanded navigation, and narrow/mobile layout on the refreshed application.

invariants.statement: Navigation authorization and canonical ordering continue to come from availableWorkspaceDestinations; collapse changes presentation only.
No contextual information is discarded: it is absent from the icon rail and available immediately after expansion.
Only a user-triggered sidebar-width change may animate; workspace route changes remain transition-free.

forbidden_states.statement: Collapsed mode hides a permitted destination, logout, the active indication, an accessible label, or the expand control.
The icon rail or its collapse toggle appears below the shared 1080px breakpoint.
The page keeps its expanded offset or clips/overflows after the rail changes width.
Navigating to another workspace destination, including Kanban, resets the selected sidebar mode or introduces a route animation.

inputs.statement: Viewport dimensions, reduced-motion preference, current route, and verified authorized destinations.

outputs.statement: The shared desktop sidebar width, icon/label presentation, active state, contextual content visibility, and available page width.
Accessible tooltips, semantics, focus, and activation for the toggle and icon-only navigation actions.

failure_semantics.statement: Focused workspace-shell widget tests fail if toggle, rail width, content width, tooltips/semantics, breakpoint behavior, reduced motion, or cross-route state retention deviate from the acceptance criteria.

argv: desktop sidebar collapses to an accessible icon-only rail and retains state across Kanban navigation

baseline_output_contains: desktop sidebar collapses to an accessible icon-only rail and retains state across Kanban navigation
